subject.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config

question: Should the supported upgrade contract reject legacy persisted `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` and have Doctor disable affected OTLP telemetry until the operator configures an OTLP/HTTP collector?
rationale: The implementation follows the repository’s canonical-config/Doctor-migration architecture, but whether an upgrade should silently retain disabled telemetry, choose a replacement transport, or preserve the old invalid configuration is a user-facing policy choice that tests cannot settle.

options.title: Adopt Doctor repair and disable affected telemetry
options.body: Merge the branch’s conservative contract: remove `grpc`, keep stdout-only logs when they do not need OTLP, and require an operator to configure HTTP export before re-enabling affected telemetry.

options.title: Preserve the legacy setting until manual migration
options.body: Keep `grpc` accepted or runtime-tolerated temporarily, then define a longer deprecation window instead of making existing configurations invalid now.

options.title: Implement gRPC support first
options.body: Retain the existing public config value and add a real gRPC exporter path before narrowing the schema.

recommendation.title: Adopt Doctor repair and disable affected telemetry
recommendation.body: Merge the branch’s conservative contract: remove `grpc`, keep stdout-only logs when they do not need OTLP, and require an operator to configure HTTP export before re-enabling affected telemetry.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is product and upgrade policy; the PR timeline directly routes this review to this candidate.
